research_question: Among aligned historical ObjectNav failures that terminate before horizon, what Actor-end dynamics precede the executed termination: early high termination prior, later search-triggered rise, low-probability stochastic end, or a mixed/no-clear pattern?
hypothesis: H-PRIOR / H-SEARCH-TRIGGERED / H-STOCHASTIC are competing observational morphologies; the audit must not assume safety alignment or representation failure is the cause.
competing_explanation: H-MIXED: sub-horizon failures may contain heterogeneous mechanisms, and video-rendered probability quantization, stochastic sampling, task difficulty, reset state, language, or scene factors may explain individual cases.
reference: Aligned historical 2026-08-03 full-200 run: 173/200 successes, 27 failures, 16 sub-horizon failures; one audited illegal end with p(end)≈0.993365 and one opposite 600-step sub120 trace with rendered p(done)<~0.018 throughout. Official ObjectNav reward config has zero failed-stop/step/horizon reward and +10 success reward, making but not proving an early-exit incentive.
repeat_or_treatment: Zero-rollout observational audit of existing historical videos/tables. Confirm final end actions for all 16 sub-horizon failures, recover quantized p(end) traces, and compare to one expert_length-nearest historical success control per case. No treatment.
unique_variable: Primary analysis contrast is termination-time dynamics within confirmed invalid-end failures and versus deterministic expert_length-nearest successful controls; no policy/environment variable is manipulated.
fixed_conditions: Use only aligned historical 2026-08-03 full-200 artifacts
Start from all 16 eps_len<600 failures; no category/size/house preselection
Confirm final executed action from video before labeling invalid-end
Use the validated video-rendered probability extraction semantics; zero bar means below ~1/55 resolution, not true zero
No simulator, model/checkpoint load, new episode, Actor forward, hidden-state Probe, replay, reset treatment, or action rewrite
expert_length is only a long-horizon matching proxy
sub_house_id is original dataset sample index, not house identity or difficulty
Carry narrow==broad target-scope status; do not overinterpret narrow visibility when scope is ambiguous
Do not infer SafeRL causation, cost-critic gating, deliberate scene-specific training, or data leakage from termination morphology alone
metrics: Matched-success p(end) in the corresponding early window
Target-scope EXACT/AMBIGUOUS and historical narrow visibility/room fields as descriptive context
expected_result: The experiment should select one next causal branch only if a clear termination morphology is observed; otherwise it should explicitly return NO_CLEAR_TERMINATION_PATTERN rather than forcing a mechanism.
falsifying_result: Any single leading termination hypothesis is weakened if the 16 confirmed sub-horizon failures are heterogeneous or matched successes show similar p(end) dynamics.
alternative_explanations: Rendered action probabilities are quantized and sub-resolution mass is invisible
Stochastic sampling can execute non-argmax actions
Instruction template, house geometry, initial distance, and long-horizon task difficulty remain confounds
narrow/broad target-ID mismatch can contaminate no-target-evidence interpretation
expert_length is an incomplete difficulty proxy
Cross-episode reset/counter state remains an open confound for later hidden-state interpretation
Observed termination dynamics do not identify whether the cause is IL, RL, SafeRL, reward design, data distribution, or implementation
stop_conditions: Fewer than 12 of 16 candidate failure traces can be recovered reliably
Action schema or row-to-action mapping cannot be frozen
Final action or p(end) extraction is ambiguous
Completion would require simulator/model execution, hidden-state Probe, replay, reset treatment, or behavior intervention
